bug_description.original: Project: skia Fuzzer: afl_skia_api_raster_n32_canvas Fuzz target binary: api_raster_n32_canvas Job Type: afl_asan_skia Crash Type: Global-buffer-overflow READ 4 Crash Address: 0x000001d8dd58 Crash State: SkPathPriv::OppositeFirstDirection SkPath::transform FuzzPath Sanitizer: address (ASAN). Detailed report: https://oss-fuzz.com/testcase?key=5765837659570176
bug_description.normalized: OSS-Fuzz issue 10323: skia global-buffer-overflow (READ of size 4) in SkPathPriv::OppositeFirstDirection, reached from SkPath::transform via the FuzzPath path-op interpreter. The fuzzer materialized an out-of-range SkPath::Direction enum from input bytes; that value was cached as SkPath::fFirstDirection and later used to index the 3-element gOppositeDir[] lookup table, reading past its end.

source.value_from: Untrusted fuzzer input byte decoded directly into an SkPath::Direction enum. SkPath::Direction is a one-byte enum with only two valid members (kCW_Direction=0, kCCW_Direction=1), but fuzz->next() fills the whole byte, so any value 0..255 is admitted. This is the load of the vulnerability-relevant value; the enum byte is the untrusted artifact and there is no deeper project parse of it.
source.description: The path-op interpreter reads a raw SkPath::Direction enum from the fuzz byte stream and passes it, unvalidated, to path->addRect(). Equivalent unranged reads exist in the sibling add* cases (addOval/addRoundRect/addRRect/addCircle, lines 94/104/113/117/121); addRect (case 13) is the representative admission point.

sink.description: Global-buffer-overflow READ of size 4: gOppositeDir[] is a static const array of 3 FirstDirection (int) entries, indexed by dir. When dir holds the out-of-range value cached in fFirstDirection, the index reads past the end of the global array (crash address 32 bytes to the left of a neighboring string literal).

root_cause.description: The fuzzer passes an out-of-range SkPath::Direction enum into the library without restricting it to the two valid members. SkPath::addRect/addOval store that raw value into the cached fFirstDirection field (SkPath::addRect at src/core/SkPath.cpp:1028; the only runtime guard, assert_known_direction at src/core/SkPath.cpp:1013, is a debug-only SkASSERT compiled out of the release/ASan build). The fix range-limits the enum at the fuzzer (fuzz->nextRange(&ui, 0, 1); dir = static_cast<SkPath::Direction>(ui);) so only {kCW,kCCW} can reach the library.

parser_admitted.note: Input was admitted by fuzz_RasterN32Canvas -> fuzz_canvas dispatch and entered the FuzzPath path-op interpreter; the per-op switch decodes the operation stream that drives SkPath construction and the later transform() call.

tainted_value_origin.description: Raw untrusted origin: a single fuzz input byte is materialized into the SkPath::Direction enum variable dir with no range restriction.

coarse_trace.summary: Fuzz entry: wraps the input bytes in a Fuzz reader and calls fuzz_RasterN32Canvas.
Sets up an N32 raster canvas and dispatches into fuzz_canvas to interpret canvas operations.
Decodes a canvas op that builds an SkPath and invokes FuzzPath to run the path-op interpreter.
Path-op interpreter reads an out-of-range SkPath::Direction from input, stores it as fFirstDirection via add*, then calls path->transform().
transform() loads the cached fFirstDirection and, on a negative-determinant matrix, passes it to OppositeFirstDirection.
Indexes the 3-element gOppositeDir[] global with the out-of-range direction: global-buffer-overflow READ of size 4.

fine_trace.note: Untrusted input read: a fuzz byte is decoded into the SkPath::Direction enum dir. The one-byte enum admits any value 0..255, but only kCW_Direction(0)/kCCW_Direction(1) are valid.

Root cause: the unvalidated, out-of-range Direction is handed to the library. The fix inserts a clamp (fuzz->nextRange(&ui,0,1); dir = static_cast<SkPath::Direction>(ui);) immediately before this call. The valid-range guard is missing here.

The out-of-range dir is cast to FirstDirection and cached in the SkPath's fFirstDirection field. assert_known_direction(dir) at src/core/SkPath.cpp:1013 is a debug-only SkASSERT and does not reject it in the ASan build.
A later op (case 29) invokes SkPath::transform on the same path, whose fFirstDirection now holds the poisoned value.
The out-of-range value is not kUnknown_FirstDirection, so the else branch is taken and the direction is forwarded instead of being reset.
On a negative-determinant matrix (det2x2 < 0), the cached fFirstDirection is loaded and passed as the index argument to OppositeFirstDirection.

Sink: gOppositeDir[] holds 3 int entries; indexing it with the out-of-range dir reads 4 bytes past the array's bounds (global-buffer-overflow READ 4). The missing valid-range guard from step 2 is what allows dir to exceed 2.

sanitizer_ground_truth.global_variable: gOppositeDir[] (static const in SkPathPriv::OppositeFirstDirection); ASan reports the OOB address 32 bytes left of a neighboring string literal at src/core/SkPath.cpp:2144 and 29 bytes right of one at src/core/SkPath.cpp:2137

poc.trigger: Fed to the api_raster_n32_canvas target on stdin (or as a file argument): /out/api_raster_n32_canvas < poc. The 37-byte input drives fuzz_RasterN32Canvas -> fuzz_canvas -> FuzzPath, selecting an add* op with an out-of-range Direction byte followed by a transform op with a negative-determinant matrix.

format.name: skia api_raster_n32_canvas fuzzer input (afl_skia_api_raster_n32_canvas)
format.contract: Opaque byte stream consumed sequentially by the Skia Fuzz reader. To be reachability-comparable it must be admitted by fuzz_RasterN32Canvas -> fuzz_canvas and reach the FuzzPath path-op interpreter, then (1) drive an add-with-direction op (addRect/addOval/addRoundRect/addRRect/addCircle) whose direction byte decodes to an out-of-range SkPath::Direction (> kCCW_Direction), so fFirstDirection is cached out of range, and (2) drive a transform op whose matrix has a negative 2x2 determinant, so SkPath::transform calls OppositeFirstDirection and indexes gOppositeDir[] out of bounds. Byte offsets are position-dependent on the preceding op stream.
